newsitem.title: USA: US, Japan insurance talks "useful", USTR's Shapiro.
newsitem.headline: US, Japan insurance talks "useful", USTR's Shapiro.

text.p: Talks between the United States and Japan on opening up the Japanese insurance market have so far been "useful," U.S. Trade Representative Ira Shapiro said Friday.
The two-day talks which started Friday were taking a break after about three hours of discussions and were to reconvene later Friday night, Shapiro told reporters.
Officials from both Japan and the United States declined to comment on the progress of the talks.
"I am not commenting on the content," said Eisuke Sakakibara, chief negotiator for Japan's Finance Ministry.
Negotiators said no time had been set for resumption of the talks on Friday. Sakakibara said the talks were expected to continue Saturday.
"It's always a pleasure to get together on insurance," Shapiro said.

Earlier, a U.S. trade official, speaking on condition he not be identified, said the United States would make "strong efforts" to resolve a long-simmering dispute with Japan over insurance during the trade talks in San Francisco.

The United States wants Japan to live up to a 1994 agreement that calls for deregulation of the primary sector dominated by big Japanese firms before deregulation of the so-called third sector of specialty insurance, which is dominated by foreign companies.
Japan's domestic insurance market is valued at about $382 billion.
